# Third-party skills

Skills by other people, vendored so they are pinned, diffable, and available without hunting for the
source. **None of this is my work.** Each folder credits its author, keeps its original `LICENSE`, and
records the upstream commit it came from.

| Collection | Author | Skills | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| [deanpeters-product-manager-skills](./deanpeters-product-manager-skills) | [Dean Peters](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills) (Productside) | 12 | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 |
| [digidai-product-manager-skills](./digidai-product-manager-skills) | [Gene Dai](https://github.com/Digidai/product-manager-skills) | 1 (large, multi-part) | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 |
| [obra-elements-of-style](./obra-elements-of-style) | [Jesse Vincent](https://github.com/obra/the-elements-of-style) | 1 | Public domain |
| [obra-superpowers](./obra-superpowers) | [Jesse Vincent](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) | 14 | MIT |

See also [`../anthropic/`](../anthropic) — 13 skills from Anthropic under Apache 2.0, same vendoring pattern,
kept separate because the license differs.

## A note on CC BY-NC-SA

The two product-management collections here are Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0.
(`obra-elements-of-style` is public domain and `obra-superpowers` is MIT — none of this section applies
to either.) Redistribution with
attribution is exactly what that license allows, which is why they can live here. The **NonCommercial** term
restricts *use*, not hosting — if you are reaching for one of these inside a job, read the license terms
yourself first. I am not a lawyer and this note is not legal advice.

## Keeping these current

Each folder is a pinned snapshot, not a live mirror. Updating means a fresh vendor commit against a newer
upstream SHA — never an edit in place, so the diff always shows what actually changed upstream.
